meta.title: Ondra First-Meet Script
meta.description: A first-meeting script for Ondra (L9 extension pool): the first encounter is cut into five beats — arrival, self-introduction, boundaries, invitation, settling. Each beat carries only an intent, the things that must be done, the things that are forbidden, and a sentence cap. It never writes a single line of dialogue: the moment this package starts composing sentences, the persona gains a second voice, and that voice never passes through the frozen prefix or the nine-step filter. Boundaries deliberately come before the invitation — say what I will not do, then ask the first question; the other order turns the first sentence into a demand. Reading never advances the waterline; only the side that actually spoke a beat may advance it, so a shell may poll as often as it likes without swallowing a beat. When the user speaks first, the script jumps straight to the settling beat instead of forcing the remaining lines. The state file holds only the beat waterline and timestamps and never a single word the user said — people give their real name and situation on the first day, and that belongs to the memory system with its own visibility rules and right to be forgotten. It does not produce the first message (that is O-045), it never sends anything on its own (that is O-042), and it never renders UI.
